style: A gothic epic oil painting of Caesar's wars in Gaul, 58 BC, in the manner of Jean-Paul Laurens, Gustave Doré and John Martin, with the classical Greco-Roman gravity of the Italian Renaissance: vast dark sky and smoke dwarfing the people, a single fierce source of light — fire, torch or moon — figures emerging from deep shadow, grim, solemn and tragic, sculptural forms, rich glazed reds and golds against darkness, a polished academic old-master finish. Roman legionaries in mail shirts, bronze Montefortino helmets and curved oval shields; Gauls with long hair, moustaches, checked trousers, cloaks and torcs. One single painting filling the whole 16:9 frame, no text, signature, border or black bars.

people.caesar: Julius Caesar, lean, bald crown with thin hair combed forward, clean-shaven, red general's cloak over a bronze muscled cuirass
people.divico: Divico, an aged Helvetian war-leader with long white hair and a long white moustache, gold torc, checked cloak
people.dumnorix: Dumnorix of the Aedui, long fair hair, drooping moustache, gold torc, rich checked cloak
people.divitiacus: Divitiacus, an Aeduan druid with long grey-brown hair and a moustache, white robe, gold torc

beats.text: At dusk the Helvetii leave their homeland for ever: from a high hillside, a long column of covered wagons, oxen and families winds away along a valley road; behind them twelve towns and their granaries burn, a vast column of smoke and glowing embers rising into a dark storm sky. The people are small; the fire and the sky dominate. Roman legionaries wear mail shirts, bronze Montefortino helmets and curved oval shields; Gauls have long hair, moustaches, checked trousers, cloaks and torcs.
